title: Audit Tabs in Saved Text
goal: Read one UTF-8 text file or standard input and report the total number of tab characters, the number of lines containing at least one tab, and the one-based line numbers of those lines. Treat the input as read-only data; do not execute or modify it.
intro: Use this small Rust 2021 CLI to spot tab characters in saved text. It accepts one file path or `-` for standard input, validates the complete input as UTF-8, and prints a concise report. Its focus on tab locations is distinct from general line counts, word lengths, first-character grouping, and line-ending audits.
requirements: Use only the Rust standard library; no external crates, unsafe code, include macros, environment variables, subprocesses, networking, or filesystem writes.
Accept exactly one CLI argument: a UTF-8 file path or `-` for stdin.
Read input without modifying or executing it, and reject invalid UTF-8 instead of silently replacing or truncating bytes.
Count every tab character and report one-based line numbers for lines containing tabs.
Write the report to stdout and actionable failures to stderr; use a nonzero exit status for failures.
Use Rust 1.90.0 with edition 2021 as the intended runner, without claiming a tested minimum version.
limits: The program reads the entire input into memory before validating UTF-8 and producing results.
Line numbers are based on splitting at LF; a final LF creates an empty final segment, which cannot contain a tab.
The tool only counts the literal tab character U+0009; it does not infer visual indentation or expand tabs.
The input is treated as data only; this program does not parse document formats or interpret commands.
Invalid-byte rejection requires a fixture containing raw invalid UTF-8 bytes. JSON text fixtures alone cannot demonstrate this case.
steps: Run `./recipe path/to/saved.txt` to audit a file, or `./recipe -` and provide text on standard input.
Check stdout for total tab count, affected-line count, and one-based line numbers; check stderr if the command reports a failure.
checks: Pipe the synthetic example input to `./recipe -` and compare stdout exactly with the expected output.
Try input containing no tabs and confirm the report says `tabs: 0`, `lines_with_tabs: 0`, and `line_numbers: none`.

For the JSON-text fixture runner, test valid Unicode text including café and €; do not claim invalid-byte rejection from a UTF-8 JSON string. A separate raw-byte test must use byte 0xFF, expect exit 2 and stderr containing input is not valid UTF-8.
Invoke the program with zero or two arguments and confirm stderr gives the usage form and the process exits nonzero.
usage: Intended runner: Rust 1.90.0, edition 2021. Save the code as `recipe.rs`, then compile with `rustc --edition=2021 recipe.rs -o recipe`. Run `./recipe <file-path>` or use `./recipe -` to read standard input. Exactly one argument is required. A file is only opened for reading. Actionable usage, I/O, and UTF-8 errors are printed to stderr with a nonzero exit status.
example_input:
Synthetic stdin text, with a literal tab between `alpha` and `beta`:
alpha	beta
plain
x	y	z
tested_scope: Executed 6 synthetic local fixture cases in isolated Rust 1.90.0 on GitHub Actions, without network access. Declared exit codes, output assertions and input integrity checks passed. Live services, installed third-party packages and production behavior remain outside scope. Editorial approval is still required.
